paths.title: Dependencies & Package Hygiene
paths.description: Choose, verify, update, and remove third-party packages safely when coding agents can suggest libraries faster than humans can assess them.

lessons.title: Prefer the standard platform
lessons.principle: Every dependency adds supply-chain and maintenance cost.
lessons.practice: Use built-in language or framework capabilities when they solve the requirement cleanly.

lessons.title: Verify package identity
lessons.principle: Models can hallucinate packages or suggest lookalikes.
lessons.practice: Check the official registry, publisher, repository, documentation, and package name before installing.

lessons.title: Assess maintenance health
lessons.principle: Popularity alone does not guarantee sustainability.
lessons.practice: Review release recency, issue activity, supported runtimes, maintainers, and deprecation notices.

lessons.title: Check licensing
lessons.principle: A technically suitable package may be legally incompatible.
lessons.practice: Review license terms and organization policy before adoption.

lessons.title: Pin reproducibly
lessons.principle: Floating versions make builds change without source changes.
lessons.practice: Use lockfiles and appropriate version constraints; pin critical build inputs more tightly.

lessons.title: Review lockfile diffs
lessons.principle: Transitive changes may be larger than the requested package.
lessons.practice: Inspect added packages, unexpected upgrades, registries, and integrity metadata.

lessons.title: Minimize dependency surface
lessons.principle: Convenience libraries can introduce large trees for small features.
lessons.practice: Compare package cost with implementing a small, well-understood utility.

lessons.title: Separate dev and runtime dependencies
lessons.principle: Production should not ship tooling it does not need.
lessons.practice: Classify packages by where they execute and build artifacts accordingly.

lessons.title: Use trusted registries
lessons.principle: Registry configuration controls what code can enter builds.
lessons.practice: Restrict package sources and authenticate private registries securely.

lessons.title: Protect install scripts
lessons.principle: Package lifecycle scripts can execute arbitrary code.
lessons.practice: Understand package trust and consider safer install policies in sensitive environments.

lessons.title: Scan known vulnerabilities
lessons.principle: Dependency risk changes after merge.
lessons.practice: Use automated advisory or dependency scanning and triage findings by exploitability and exposure.

lessons.title: Update incrementally
lessons.principle: Large version jumps combine many behavioral changes.
lessons.practice: Read migration notes and update in manageable steps with tests.

lessons.title: Avoid abandoned packages
lessons.principle: Unmaintained code accumulates compatibility and security risk.
lessons.practice: Replace critical abandoned dependencies before they become blockers.

lessons.title: Remove unused packages
lessons.principle: Dead dependencies remain supply-chain and build liabilities.
lessons.practice: Periodically detect and remove packages no longer imported or required.

lessons.title: Control transitive overrides carefully
lessons.principle: Forced resolutions can create unsupported combinations.
lessons.practice: Document why overrides exist and remove them when upstream fixes arrive.

lessons.title: Verify binary and native packages
lessons.principle: Prebuilt artifacts increase platform and provenance considerations.
lessons.practice: Check supported architectures, signatures or provenance, and fallback build requirements.

lessons.title: Review SDK permissions
lessons.principle: Cloud and third-party SDKs can expose powerful APIs.
lessons.practice: Use least-privilege credentials and configure only required capabilities.

lessons.title: Track breaking changes
lessons.principle: Agent-generated upgrades may compile while subtly changing semantics.
lessons.practice: Read changelogs for auth, defaults, serialization, caching, and error behavior.

lessons.title: Automate dependency policy
lessons.principle: Manual review alone does not scale.
lessons.practice: Use bots, scanners, allowlists, and required checks appropriate to repository risk.

lessons.title: Document major dependency choices
lessons.principle: Frameworks and core libraries shape architecture for years.
lessons.practice: Record why major packages were selected, alternatives considered, and exit considerations.

codeExamples.snippet:
npm view zod name version repository license
npm audit --omit=dev
git diff -- package.json package-lock.json

paths.title: Performance & Scalability
paths.description: Keep AI-generated software responsive and efficient by measuring bottlenecks, setting budgets, and optimizing the right layer.

lessons.title: Measure before optimizing
lessons.principle: Intuition is unreliable about real bottlenecks.
lessons.practice: Profile latency, CPU, memory, network, queries, and rendering before changing architecture.

lessons.title: Set performance budgets
lessons.principle: Without thresholds, regressions accumulate gradually.
lessons.practice: Define budgets for key user and server metrics and enforce them where practical.

lessons.title: Optimize user-perceived latency
lessons.principle: Backend speed alone does not determine experience.
lessons.practice: Measure time to useful content, interaction responsiveness, and completion of important actions.

lessons.title: Avoid unbounded work
lessons.principle: Lists, loops, searches, and uploads can grow beyond expected sizes.
lessons.practice: Paginate, cap, stream, or batch work based on realistic limits.

lessons.title: Prevent N+1 queries
lessons.principle: Repeated data access is a common generated-code scaling defect.
lessons.practice: Inspect query count per request and batch related data.

lessons.title: Use indexes from workload evidence
lessons.principle: Indexes speed reads but cost writes and storage.
lessons.practice: Create indexes around real filter, join, and ordering patterns and verify query plans.

lessons.title: Cache with an invalidation model
lessons.principle: Caching without freshness rules creates correctness bugs.
lessons.practice: Define cache key, owner, lifetime, invalidation, and fallback before adding a cache.

lessons.title: Compress and minimize payloads
lessons.principle: Sending unnecessary data wastes bandwidth and parsing time.
lessons.practice: Select needed fields, paginate results, compress responses, and avoid oversized JSON.

lessons.title: Control client bundle growth
lessons.principle: AI can import large libraries for small UI needs.
lessons.practice: Track bundles and prefer selective imports, code splitting, and platform features.

lessons.title: Optimize images and media
lessons.principle: Large media often dominates page weight.
lessons.practice: Serve appropriately sized formats, responsive sources, lazy load noncritical content, and reserve dimensions.

lessons.title: Avoid blocking the main thread
lessons.principle: Long JavaScript tasks make interfaces feel frozen.
lessons.practice: Split heavy work, use workers when justified, and minimize synchronous computation during interaction.

lessons.title: Use concurrency deliberately
lessons.principle: Parallel work helps only when dependencies and limits permit it.
lessons.practice: Bound concurrency to protect databases, APIs, memory, and rate limits.

lessons.title: Use backpressure
lessons.principle: Producers can overwhelm slower consumers.
lessons.practice: Apply queue limits, streaming flow control, or admission limits under load.

lessons.title: Load test critical paths
lessons.principle: Unit performance does not predict whole-system contention.
lessons.practice: Test representative traffic, concurrency, data size, and failure conditions.

lessons.title: Profile memory
lessons.principle: Leaks and retained data can crash long-running processes.
lessons.practice: Inspect heap growth, caches, subscriptions, listeners, and unbounded collections.

lessons.title: Design autoscaling signals
lessons.principle: CPU alone may not reflect workload pressure.
lessons.practice: Scale on metrics related to queue depth, concurrency, latency, or resource saturation.

lessons.title: Protect dependencies under load
lessons.principle: Scaling the frontend tier can overload databases or third parties.
lessons.practice: Use connection limits, rate controls, caching, queues, and circuit behavior.

lessons.title: Test cold starts and warmup
lessons.principle: Serverless and container workloads can behave differently after idle periods.
lessons.practice: Measure initialization and reduce heavy startup or provide capacity where latency matters.

lessons.title: Observe tail latency
lessons.principle: Averages can hide severe slow experiences.
lessons.practice: Track percentiles such as p95 or p99 for important operations.

lessons.title: Re-measure after optimization
lessons.principle: An optimization is only successful if evidence improves without unacceptable tradeoffs.
lessons.practice: Compare before and after metrics and watch for correctness, cost, or complexity regressions.

codeExamples.snippet:
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT p.id, p.title
FROM project p
WHERE p.workspace_id = $1
ORDER BY p.updated_at DESC
LIMIT 50;
